explanation.headline: Raise 2.5x was the top play, and you found it.

paragraphs: You held K♣ 5♦ in the big blind, against Villain, a LAG player, on the button. Pre-flop, Villain opened to 2.5 bb. You faced 1.5 bb more to call, with 3.5 bb in the pot.
sections.title: The hand

paragraphs: You chose Raise 2.5x (EV 0.9 bb), the top play against Villain's range. Verdict: Best.

Your equity against Villain's whole range is 51.2%. Calling 1.5 bb into a pot of 3.5 bb needs 1.5 bb / (3.5 bb + 1.5 bb) = 30.0% equity. Out of position you realise only 80% of your 51.2% equity, which makes 41.0%: that is above what it needs, so calling would beat folding.

Raise 2.5x: Villain folds 41% of the time, less than the 58.8% a raise this size needs to profit on folds alone (5 bb / (3.5 bb + 5 bb)), so folds alone don't pay for it: it relies on your 44.0% equity against the hands that continue.
Right now you are ahead of 66.1% of Villain's range.
sections.title: The verdict

paragraphs: Villain is a LAG player. Loose-aggressive: wide ranges, frequent pressure, more bluffs.
Villain's range narrowed with each action: Pre-flop: opens to 2.5 bb.
